clue.text: Drop brush

definitions.meaning: to drop a plan is to cancel or abandon it
brush is low scrubby vegetation, undergrowth

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: abandoning a plan, and an area of stunted bushes and undergrowth.

clue.text: Buy the drinks, having drunk gallons, and don't sway!

indicators.note: the drinks phrase swallows the next piece, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: to buy a round of drinks for everyone is to stand one's round

explanation.surface: A pub-goer, after many gallons, is urged to pay for a round and stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The round of drinks takes in a G, turning ROUND into GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to sway or give way under pressure is holding firm, an idiom for staying put.

clue.text: Bird's beak and yellow back

indicators.note: placed at the end, back says the pair of words is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nib is a bird's beak
OR is the heraldic tincture gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A description of a bird with a yellow beak and back.
explanation.definitionFit: A robin is a common small songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: One may be charged with a criminal offence

definitions.meaning: an electrical cell is something that gets charged up

explanation.surface: Someone may be charged with a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cell takes an electrical charge; the same word names the crime of unlawful physical attack.

clue.text: Tries his cooking before wife produces a dish

indicators.note: the mixed letters come in front of the next piece in the answer
cooking the books means tampering, so the letters of these two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man tries his hand at cooking before his wife serves a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutton, potato and onion stew from Ireland is a well-known dish.

clue.text: Edible seaweed served up in club

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nori is the edible seaweed used to wrap sushi

explanation.surface: Seaweed served at a club's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with an angled metal head is called by this name.

clue.text: Lagging home unit also in need of repair

parts.note: at home is in, so IN stands for home

indicators.note: broken and needing to be fixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The lagging in a home unit needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of repair' rearranges UNITALSO into SULATION. Lagging here is the noun, padding on pipes, not falling behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging is material wrapped round pipes and tanks to stop heat escaping.

clue.text: Rugby players call girls

definitions.meaning: in rugby the forward who hooks the ball in the scrum has this name

explanation.surface: Rugby players phone some women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' looks like a verb, but 'call girls' is one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby position named for hooking the ball back, and slang for prostitutes.

clue.text: Excite one with work being shown in gallery

indicators.note: an exhibit is displayed inside the gallery, so the pieces go inside it

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
I is the Roman numeral one
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: An exciting artwork is on show in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is London's famous gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to arouse or stimulate interest, often mildly erotically.

clue.text: In great suspense, having reportedly provoked sappers in spa town

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with money

indicators.note: says the word for provoked is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: baited means teased or provoked

indicators.note: the engineers go inside the town

parts.note: Bath is the English spa town
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Someone provoked soldiers stationed in a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bated, from abated, means held back; BATH is an English spa city famous for its Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding one's breath while waiting anxiously is the idiom for great suspense.

clue.text: What was shot? Golf course achievement accounting for handicap

definitions.meaning: the Ancient Mariner shot a seabird in Coleridge's poem
a hole played three under par
a burden, as in a millstone round one's neck

explanation.surface: A golfer's question about a shot and a great score given their handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: the bird shot in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, a golf score three under par, and a burdensome encumbrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird killed in Coleridge's poem, a rare golf score, and a burden all share this name.

clue.text: Group round court, extremely elegant

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the extremes of the word elegant are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A group gathers round a court, looking very elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers or items is a group.

clue.text: Duke's exclusive formal evening meal

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
an inner circle is exclusive

explanation.surface: A duke hosts a select, formal evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal eaten in the evening, especially a formal one, is supper.

clue.text: Choir bringing joy to nightspot

parts.note: glee is joy
a nightclub is a nightspot

explanation.surface: A choir brings joy to a nightclub audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A society of singers performing short part-songs is a choir.

clue.text: Studies infringement of copyright scheme

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
illegal copying is called piracy

explanation.surface: Studies show copyright infringement is a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plot or plan by a group is a scheme.

clue.text: Billy's mate, the one looking after the kids?

definitions.meaning: a billy is a male goat, whose mate is a female goat

definitions.text: the one looking after the kids?
definitions.meaning: a nanny looks after children; kids are also young goats

explanation.definitionFit: The female goat mates with the billy, and as mother tends the young goats, punning on a children's nurse.

clue.text: Hitchcock film noir, too blinking American

indicators.note: blinking is a mild curse, and a word in a blinking state is disordered, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a Hitchcock noir as too American.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock directed the 1946 spy film of this name with Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Small trading centre, well-kept

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A small, tidy marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means neat and tidy in appearance, as well-kept things are.

clue.text: Arrangement promoted on television

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a television is a set
up means raised or promoted

explanation.surface: An arrangement is promoted on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is the way something is organised or laid out.

clue.text: Detailed decorative design around large dish

indicators.note: the trimmed design goes around the next piece
de-tailed: the design word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: a pattern is a decorative design

explanation.surface: A large dish with a detailed decorative pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' cuts PATTERN to PATTER; 'around' puts that round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving plate is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Old golf club having supply may make one overindulge

parts.note: a spoon was an old lofted wooden golf club
to feed is to supply

explanation.surface: A golfer with plenty of supplies might overindulge.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOON is a historical golf club, roughly a modern three-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon-feeding someone pampers them, giving so much that they are over-indulged.

clue.text: Under 50%, certainly

definitions.meaning: less than one half, taken literally
British slang exclamation meaning very much so

explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the phrase is an emphatic yes: 'Did you enjoy it?' 'Not half!'
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, less than one half; as British slang, an emphatic agreement meaning absolutely.

clue.text: Unusual person, artist, meeting another, a viscount

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
another Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An unusual person: an artist meeting another artist and a viscount.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for rare bird, used of an exceptional or unusual person.

clue.text: Showing a profit in mine mostly causes a state of shock

indicators.note: the profit word goes inside the shortened store
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a mine of information is a store
a business that is up is showing a profit

explanation.surface: Showing a profit in a mine leaves someone in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STORE to STOR, with UP put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition where one can barely think or react.

clue.text: Made from recipes, tomato sauce

indicators.note: the answer is made from letters running across these two words

explanation.surface: A tomato sauce made from recipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, pine nut and cheese sauce.

clue.text: A fish — jelly?

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Is a fish a jelly?
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set food and culture microbes.

clue.text: Vessel about to be destroyed

indicators.note: the word about is wrecked, its letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship is about to be destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Area around Greece, area for example Aeneas sacked

indicators.note: as Troy was sacked, the hero's name is ravaged, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Aeneas, fleeing the sacking of Troy, crosses the waters near Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey is the water around Greece.

clue.text: Saboteur in warship

explanation.surface: A saboteur aboard a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wrecks things, and a fast, small naval warship of that name.

clue.text: Father's hot stew bubbles

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: to stew is to cook slowly, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Father's hot stew bubbles on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is a mass of small bubbles on a liquid.
